title: Items
text:
Selecting the Item ID will take you to a page displaying the question, answer, and (if available) worked solutions and other notes.
Clicking the Stem can be used to quickly preview a question, but may not show all elements (e.g., graphs, mathmatical text, etc.).
The TXT column shows the question and answer in raw text format for easy copying and pasting.
The Export checkbox allows instructors to mark questions for export and generate a consolidated plain-text file for easy copying into an Canvas. Because the export is just raw text, images are not included.
The R Exam column provides the item’s R Markdown code for any instructors using the “exams R package”. This package enables you to do things like:

Randomize question order and question elements (e.g., values, names, etc.)
Display corresponing graphs, and other diagrams
Generate multiple exam versions automatically
Export exams to different formats (Canvas, Word documents, Webpages, PDFs, and more)

Note: This approach requires solid knowledge of R and the exams package.

title: Item 4
text:
Include in export 

A researcher had five different groups of rats in an experiment. Each group of rats was given a different dosage of caffeine. The number of rats in each group and their dosage in milligrams (mg) is below. What was the mean dose of caffeine across all the rats?



Group
Rats
Dose




Control
14
0


A
9
4


B
11
8


C
6
16


D
15
32




Correct Answer
12.72727


Solution:
The mean dose is 12.73 mg (rounded to two decimal places).
This is a weighted mean problem, where each dose is weighted by the number of rats receiving that dose.
The formula is: \[\bar{x} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n} w_i x_i}{\sum_{i=1}^{n} w_i}\]
Calculating: \[
\begin{align}
\bar{x}
&= \frac{14 \times 0 + 9 \times 4 + 11 \times 8 + 6 \times 16 + 15 \times 32}{14 + 9 + 11 + 6 + 15} \\[0.5em]
&= \frac{0 + 36 + 88 + 96 + 480}{55} \\[0.5em]
&= \frac{700}{55} \\[0.5em]
&= 12.727\overline{27}
\end{align}
\]
R code:
x <- c(0, 4, 8, 16, 32)   # doses in mg
w <- c(14, 9, 11, 6, 15)  # number of rats (weights)

weighted_mean <- sum(x * w) / sum(w)
weighted_mean

title: Item 2
text:
Include in export 

\(\Phi\) is a very sacred number called the “Golden Ratio”. Some people believe that it has magick properties which allow us, mere mortals, to understand more than just the natural world. It is approximately equal to:
1.6180339887498948482045868343656381177203091798057
Including the 1 preceding the decimal, what is the mode of the first 21 digits of \(\Phi\)?

Correct Answer
8


Solution:
Counting the frequency of each digit, the most frequently occurring digit is 8, therefore the mode is 8.

title: Home
text:
This site is a working example of an outcome-aligned course database. Its purpose is to demonstrate how learning outcomes, assessment items, and instructional resources can be organized within a single framework for new and current instructors of PSYCH 213.
Use the navigation bar to browse Outcomes, Resources, and Items.
The site requires minimal ongoing curation, as most of its content is generated automatically using using . Updates typically involve little more than editing a spreadsheet and adding new files for questions or local resources (e.g., datasets).

title: Item 1
text:
Include in export 

A student scored the following percentages on their end of the year exams:

Alchemy: 47
Astrology: 32
Falconry: 37
Logic: 89
Music: 56
Swordsmanship: 35
Tarot: 46
Xylomancy: 34

What was their mean score?

Correct Answer
47


Solution:
The mean score is calculated as:
\[\frac{\sum x}{N} = \frac{47 + 32 + 37 + 89 + 56 + 35 + 46 + 34}{8} = \frac{376}{8} = 47\]
R Code:
x <- c(47, 32, 37, 89, 56, 35, 46, 34)
mean(x)

title: Item 3
text:
Include in export 

Which of the following is a valid way to label a sample mean? Select all that apply.

\(\sigma\)
\(\bar{x}\)
\(\bar{y}\)
\(\hat{x}\)
\(\mu\)


Correct Answer
FALSE TRUE TRUE FALSE FALSE


Solution:
The correct answers are \(\bar{y}\) and \(\bar{x}\).
Sample means are denoted using bar notation (e.g., \(\bar{x}\) or \(\bar{y}\)), where the bar over the variable indicates the mean of the sample data.
Why the other options are incorrect:

\(\mu\) (mu) is the symbol for the population mean, not the sample mean. Greek letters are reserved for population parameters.
\(\hat{x}\) (x-hat) typically represents a predicted or fitted value in regression analysis, not a sample mean. While both are estimates, they serve different purposes.
\(\sigma\) (sigma) is the symbol for the population standard deviation, not a measure of central tendency.

Key distinction: Sample statistics use Roman letters with special notation (like the bar), while population parameters use Greek letters.

title: Item 5
text:
Include in export 

Destinee rolled two six-sided die and plotted their values on the histogram below. What percentage of the rolls were either a 6, 7, or 8?


Correct Answer
35


Solution:
Each bar shows the number of times a certain value was rolled. Therefore the total percentage of rolls for 6, 7, and 8 is . . .
\[
\begin{align}
\text{Percent} &=
\frac{2+1+4}{1+2+3+1+2+1+4+2+2+2} \times 100 \\[0.5em]
&= \frac{7}{20} \times 100 \\[0.5em]
&= 35.00
\end{align}
\]

R Code:
freq_678 <- c(2, 1, 4)
freq_tot <- c(1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 1, 4, 2, 2, 2)

sum(freq_678) / sum(freq_tot) * 100
